clue.text: English bobby in helmet? A cool dude

indicators.note: the bobby and the English letter sit inside the headgear, as a head sits in a helmet

parts.note: a helmet is a kind of hat, the question mark flagging the example
a bobby is a British policeman, a police constable, PC

explanation.surface: A British policeman in his helmet is asked whether he is a cool customer.
explanation.walkthrough: The bobby's helmet looks like part of the scene, but it is simply a hat, and the British police constable (PC) goes inside it with E.
explanation.definitionFit: Old jazz-era slang for a stylish, hip person, someone cool and in the know.

clue.text: Occupied, showing purpose — good time to get stuck in

indicators.note: the good and time pieces are pushed into the middle of the purpose word, stuck inside it

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone busy and purposeful is told it is a good time to get stuck in to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a phone line or toilet that is in use is busy, taken by someone.

clue.text: Worker in firm produces piece of poetry

indicators.note: the worker is placed within the firm, as an employee is in a company

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: An employee in a company turns out a bit of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A canto is a major division of a long poem, as in Dante's Divine Comedy.

clue.text: Fighters moved very quickly, pursued by a blonde bombshell

indicators.note: in this down clue the hurrying piece comes first, followed by the rest, as if chased

parts.note: to tear along is to rush; past tense tore
Diana Dors was the 1950s British film star billed as the blonde bombshell

explanation.surface: Fighters rush off, chased by a glamorous blonde.
explanation.walkthrough: Diana Dors was a British actress, Britain's answer to Marilyn Monroe, nicknamed the blonde bombshell.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullfighters on horseback are called by this Spanish word, so they are fighters in the ring.

clue.text: Celebrity female is accompanying husband, a swimmer

parts.note: a star is a famous person, a celebrity
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogies

explanation.surface: A famous woman is seen with her husband, who is a swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: The swimmer is not the husband but a sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-armed echinoderm that moves through the sea is loosely a swimmer, a sea creature.

clue.text: Pulpits badly produced come apart

indicators.note: something badly made is out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pulpits that were poorly built fall to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to separate or break into pieces, as a couple or a cracked structure does.

clue.text: Female MP once in a never-ending rage

indicators.note: a fury with no end loses its final letter

parts.note: to storm is to rage; a storm of anger

explanation.surface: A former woman MP flies into an endless fury.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy Astor was the first woman to take her seat in the British House of Commons, in 1919.
explanation.definitionFit: Nancy, Viscountess Astor, was a pioneering woman member of Parliament in the past.

clue.text: Over-smart church sculptures? Such may be seen in lecture

definitions.text: Such may be seen in lecture

parts.note: flip means glib or flippant, too clever by half
sculptures are works of art

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at too-clever religious statues on show at a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A large pad of paper on an easel is used by speakers to illustrate a talk.

clue.text: S. Pickwick's valet, one to bulge out

definitions.meaning: Sam Weller is Mr Pickwick's servant in Dickens's Pickwick Papers, written with initial and surname
something that swells or bulges outward

explanation.surface: Pickwick's manservant is described as one who puffs out.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the initial and surname together as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing that swells, expanding outward, as the agent noun of the verb swell.

clue.text: Take lingerers apart in a situation wreaking havoc with the economy?

definitions.text: a situation wreaking havoc with the economy

indicators.note: taking the words apart breaks them up so the letters can be reassembled

explanation.surface: Dawdlers are pulled to pieces when the economy is in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage across many industries at once halts production and can wreck a nation's economy.

clue.text: I concede, having admitted small number with insufficient know-how

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the conceding word lets the small number in, holding it inside

parts.note: to grant a point is to concede it
NO is the short form of number

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to a small figure while admitting they lack expertise.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking knowledge or skill, so without enough know-how; a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Remember everyone at the sports ground

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a British public playing field
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone at the playing field is asked to remember something.
explanation.walkthrough: A rec, short for recreation ground, is a British public park for games.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to bring back to mind, to recollect something past.

clue.text: A soldier enters a party in leisurely fashion

indicators.note: the soldier piece goes into the party word, entering it

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
taken as written
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier arrives at a party in an unhurried way.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical direction meaning slowly, at a relaxed pace, from Italian.

clue.text: My acting's absurdly acrobatic

indicators.note: something done absurdly is nonsensical, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An actor admits their performance is ridiculously athletic.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: agile, showing the physical skill of a tumbler or gymnast.

clue.text: I, having taken a bash after school, must get foot treatment

indicators.note: the self-and-attempt pieces follow the school, coming after it

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
taken as written
to have a bash is to have a try

explanation.surface: A pupil, after a go at something following school, needs care for their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Chiropody, the medical care of feet, as practised by a chiropodist.

clue.text: Maybe enjoying restaurant clamour and latest taste?

parts.note: din is noise, clamour
in means fashionable, the latest thing
gout is French for taste, used in English as goût

explanation.surface: A noisy restaurant with the newest flavours is presented as something to enjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating a meal away from home, typically at a restaurant; the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: Given external stimulus, mean fellow almost made a commitment

indicators.note: the stimulus is put on the outside, wrapping round the other piece

parts.note: a prod is a nudge or spur, a stimulus

indicators.note: almost the whole word, cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a miser is a stingy person

explanation.surface: A stingy man, given a push, nearly pledged himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: gave one's word, pledged to do something.

clue.text: Go round with cleaner to get bit of food

parts.note: to roll is to turn over and over, going round
a mop is a floor-cleaning tool

explanation.surface: A cleaner is told to go round with the mop to pick up a scrap of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickled herring fillet rolled round a filling, served as a snack or appetiser.

clue.text: Red card — feature of a ball game

definitions.meaning: a card from one of the two red suits in a pack, alongside hearts
the infield of a baseball pitch, laid out as a square on its point

explanation.surface: A sending-off in football seems to be part of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red card' looks like a football referee's dismissal; it is a playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the red suits in cards, and the infield of a baseball field.

clue.text: 'Character' — a nut wandering about

indicators.note: the letters stray from their order, wandering into a new one

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A strange character is described as a nut on the loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: one's essential temperament or disposition, as in good-natured.

clue.text: One goes round rubbish dumped on a hill

indicators.note: in a down clue the rubbish sits on top of the rest, placed first

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Waste is tipped on a hillside by someone who keeps circling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that turns or spins, like a muscle or device that rotates.

clue.text: Crows left penned in by animals

indicators.note: the left letter is shut inside the animals, as in a pen

parts.note: goats are farm animals

explanation.surface: Black birds are left trapped in a pen with farm animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crows' looks like the birds; it is the verb, to boast.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to crow is to exult smugly over a success or another's failure.

clue.text: Stolen stuff's turning up in seat

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the word from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: loot is stolen goods; loot's, loot is, gives the extra S

explanation.surface: Stolen goods are found hidden in a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A backless seat for one person, a simple kind of chair.

clue.text: Refuse to accept sailor, one hiding head by entrance

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: the word for one has its first letter concealed, removed

parts.note: the number written out
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: A sailor is turned away while one ducks his head by the doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce or deny oneself something, refusing it.

clue.text: Liberal admitted to good Scottish society

indicators.note: the Liberal letter is let into the Scots word, admitted inside

parts.note: guid is the Scots form of good

explanation.surface: A Liberal is let into a respectable Scottish club.
explanation.definitionFit: An association of people with a shared trade or interest, a society.

clue.text: Some toiler got mad — a person who can tell what's in the air

definitions.text: a person who can tell what's in the air

indicators.note: the letters have gone crazy, scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A worker went crazy, as some sensitive person might sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather forecaster studies the atmosphere, so can say what conditions are in the air.

clue.text: Spotted having little kiss in winter vehicle

indicators.note: the kiss is placed within the vehicle

parts.note: a sled is a sledge for snow
a peck is a quick light kiss

explanation.surface: Someone is seen giving a quick kiss in a sledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like seen; it means dotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Marked with small dots or flecks of colour, dappled.

clue.text: Royal family exciting characters in Stroud

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A royal house's thrilling figures are found in the Gloucestershire town of Stroud.
explanation.definitionFit: The English royal dynasty of Henry VIII and Elizabeth I, a ruling house.
